The international scheme for placing scalp EEG electrodes at 10 or 20 percent distances between skull landmarks; odd numbers mark the left side, even numbers the right and Z the midline.
A maneuver during an EEG, such as hyperventilation, photic stimulation or sleep deprivation, that makes abnormal discharges more likely to appear.
The 8 to 13 Hz rhythm that dominates the posterior waking EEG with the eyes closed and fades with drowsiness.
A burst of about 14 Hz (sigma) activity on the EEG that marks entry into sleep; now a defining feature of stage N2.
Brief runs of generalized synchronous waves on the EEG; about half of patients have hepatic encephalopathy and the rest another toxic-metabolic encephalopathy.
PLEDs; periodic EEG discharges over one hemisphere that point to an acute destructive cerebral lesion.
QEEG; computer analysis of digitized EEG data compared with normative databases and shown as topographic maps; not a diagnostic test for psychiatric disorders.
The EEG response time-locked to a repeated sensory stimulus; abnormal in many conditions, so of limited use in differential diagnosis.
The study of biologic time and rhythms of all periods, from milliseconds to years.
A time cue that resets the internal clock; the main one is the daily change between light and dark.
A person's diurnal preference, from morning lark to night owl.
A circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder with sleep and waking hours earlier than desired; the chapter's advanced sleep phase syndrome. A familial form is autosomal dominant.
A circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder with sleep and waking hours later than desired; the chapter's delayed sleep phase syndrome.
